Use Tier 2: add causal history pooling inside the best balanced-BCE ConvRec, focusing on model_design and training_evaluation. Balanced BCE achieved 0.5387 macro validation HR@10, while adding attention reduced performance; this motivates preserving the convolutional backbone and testing a simpler representation of persistent user preferences. The hypothesis is that convolutional features inadequately preserve unordered interests across the available history, although the existing results do not establish this as the plateau’s cause.

Make one architectural change: fuse a masked cumulative mean of input item embeddings into the convolutional representation before final normalization. At each position, average only nonpadding embeddings up to that position, project the mean into the hidden dimension, and add it through a learned elementwise sigmoid gate conditioned on both representations. Mask padded positions and clamp the averaging denominator so empty histories remain finite. Train the pooling projection, gate, convolutional layers, item embeddings, and item bias jointly within one network per category, retaining the best trial’s balanced BCE, negative sampling, token limit, and other training settings.

Update checkpoint reconstruction and the predictor writer to include the new parameters, preserving identical forward-pass scoring during validation and host inference. Keep all four dataset routes, supplied splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts; select and reload exactly one checkpoint per category. Evaluate fixed validation HR@10 using 200 users per category, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42, print the recomputed macro average as Final Validation Score, and assess improvement against 0.5387 without accessing hidden test data or generating a local test submission.
